questions.explain: The chapter's operational pattern is detection -> reasoning -> action: telemetry feeds ML/LLM reasoning that interprets context, and parameterized executors act with appropriate scope, each layer independently testable and observable.
options: Collect, store, and visualize

Detection (metrics, query telemetry, system events), reasoning (ML models or LLM analysis that interprets context), and action (parameterized automation that executes with appropriate scope) — each layer independently testable and observable
Backup, restore, and verify
Plan, build, and deploy
questions.q: What is the three-layer intelligent automation stack the chapter describes?

questions.explain: The urgency query weights avg_fragmentation_in_percent by LOG of total reads and zeroes out tiny indexes (page_count < 100), replacing the static 30%-fragmentation threshold that over-maintains small objects and under-maintains large ones.
options: avg_fragmentation_in_percent weighted by read activity via log-scaling, discounted to 0 for indexes with fewer than 100 pages — so tiny indexes never bubble to the top of the queue
Purely by page_count, largest first
By the alphabetical order of index names
By fragmentation alone, ignoring usage
questions.q: How is the maintenance urgency_score for index maintenance computed?

questions.explain: The chapter is explicit: the LLM never writes SQL dynamically; it selects from allowed_actions and populates parameters, and the executor validates every identifier against sys.tables before running the template.
options: To reduce API costs
To execute faster

Because an LLM writing and running SQL dynamically leads to injection vulnerabilities and unpredictable behavior — templates plus identifier validation against sys.tables keep execution bounded and safe
Because SQL Server cannot execute dynamic SQL
questions.q: Why does the LLM-driven runbook executor select from a predefined action library instead of generating SQL dynamically?

questions.explain: The runbook rules state blocking REBUILDs require a lock and are never recommended during business hours; REORGANIZE is online, so it is preferred for fragmented indexes in narrow windows.
options: A blocking index REBUILD during business hours
REORGANIZE — it is an online operation, preferred for fragmented indexes in narrow maintenance windows; blocking REBUILDs are never recommended during business hours
DROP INDEX followed by CREATE INDEX
UPDATE STATISTICS only
questions.q: In a narrow maintenance window, which maintenance action does the chapter prefer for a fragmented index?

questions.explain: The confidence gate sends anything below AUTO_EXECUTE_THRESHOLD (default 0.75) to PagerDuty instead of executing; the chapter recommends new teams start at 0.90 and lower it as they build trust in the diagnosis quality.
options: 0.50 for everyone
0.99 for everyone
The default AUTO_EXECUTE_THRESHOLD is 0.75, but teams new to autonomous remediation should start at 0.90 and lower it over time as confidence in diagnosis quality builds
There is no threshold; all actions execute automatically
questions.q: What is the default confidence threshold for autonomous remediation execution, and where should teams new to autonomy start?
